claim: Actress Anne Heche, 53, crashed her car into a home in the Mar Vista neighborhood of Los Angeles on August 5, 2022; the vehicle caught fire and first responders took roughly half an hour to extricate her. She never regained consciousness, was declared brain-dead on August 11, 2022 and pronounced legally dead — kept on life support afterward only so her organs could be donated, which her family confirmed she had chosen. The Los Angeles County coroner ruled the death accidental, attributing it to inhalation and thermal injuries, with a sternal fracture from blunt trauma a significant contributing factor. Toxicology found benzoylecgonine — an inactive metabolite of cocaine indicating prior, not active, use — and concluded there was no evidence of impairment by illicit drugs at the time of the crash; the fentanyl detected was administered as hospital treatment. Heche had filmed the Lifetime movie "Girl in Room 13," about a young woman held captive and forced into sex trafficking, which aired posthumously on September 17, 2022. Aerial and ground news footage of her extrication (KTLA, CBS2/KCAL, Entertainment Tonight) circulated widely. Frame-by-frame review of that footage confirms the on-the-record detail: the sheet-covered figure on the gurney is in a raised, semi-upright posture — torso elevated, not lying flat — with the upper body and an arm shifting position as firefighters move the gurney toward the fire engine. This is consistent with the first-responder reporting that Heche was conscious and breathing when she was placed on the stretcher and transported in critical condition; she died days later at the Grossman Burn Center from an oxygen-deprived (anoxic) brain injury. The footage was nonetheless recirculated online as proof she "sat up," was secretly alive, the death was staged, or that she was silenced over the trafficking film. Being alive and moving at the scene is what the documented timeline states; it is not evidence of foul play, and the coroner ruled the death accidental.

notes: Group-B record. The crash, the ~30-minute extrication, the brain-death declaration, the organ donation, the coroner's accidental ruling, the toxicology (no impairment at the time of the crash), and the posthumous September 17, 2022 airing of 'Girl in Room 13' are all verifiable. The reel pairs the crash footage (on-screen chyron 'PERSON RESCUED AFTER CAR SLAMS INTO HOUSE') with the trafficking-film clip to imply she was targeted. First-hand frame analysis (extraction footage pulled and reviewed at 8fps): the sheet-covered figure on the gurney is genuinely in a raised, semi-upright posture with visible upper-body and arm movement as it is wheeled to the engine — the 'she sat up' observation is accurate, not fabricated. But the straight reading is the opposite of the conspiracy one: first responders reported she was conscious and breathing when placed on the stretcher, so movement at the scene is exactly what the record says happened. The anoxic brain injury and death came days later, at the burn center. Separated from interpretation per house rules: the footage is real and she was alive/moving at the scene; the 'staged / secretly alive / silenced' inference does not follow from it and the coroner ruled the death accidental.
